summary: Workday filed an 8-K on October 1, 2026, disclosing entry into a new $1.5 billion unsecured revolving Credit Agreement among Workday, subsidiary guarantors, several lenders, Wells Fargo as administrative agent, swing line lender and L/C issuer, and Bank of America, Barclays, and Morgan Stanley entities as syndication agents and joint lead arrangers/bookrunners. The facility replaces Workday's prior $1.0 billion April 6, 2022 revolver, matures October 1, 2031, permits two one-year extensions, allows penalty-free prepayment and commitment reduction, and had no outstanding borrowings at closing. This is an ordinary credit-facility refinancing, not a special situation; item 1.02 reflects termination of the replaced agreement. What to watch is pricing grid risk and subsequent revolver draws, not event-driven arbitrage.
